extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO enrollment & discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order excluding a registered patent attorney from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-court disbarment, with procedural directions, penalties, and notice/publishing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline (including exclusion from practice before the USPTO) based on disciplinary action by a state court; the Director determines whether there is a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and whether identical discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that the OED Director filed a Complaint requesting exclusion identical to the state-imposed discipline. The Director found (1) no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and (2) exclusion appropriate. References: 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity and requirement to contest within 40 days
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent seeks to contest imposition of exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the respondent believes sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted under the grounds permissible in § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order directed that the response must include all supporting information to create a genuine issue of material fact. In this case the mailed Notice and Order was returned "not deliverable," and the respondent did not file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when mail is undeliverable (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a mailed Notice and Order cannot be delivered, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b) and § 11.35(b) may be used to notify the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A service by publication notice was published in the Official Gazette on March 30, 2010 and April 6, 2010 notifying Respondent how to obtain a copy of the Notice and Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office, beginning on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs exclusion and specifies further obligations and prohibitions (see compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded and dissociation of customer numbers and PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is excluded must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the period of exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states Respondent shall comply fully with § 11.58 while excluded. (The Order also grants limited recognition to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for 30 days to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited recognition to practice before the Office may be granted beginning on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating the respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is time-limited and is only for compliance with the specified subsection (e.g., informing clients and transferring matters as required by § 11.58(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate the respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate administrative step ordered by the USPTO to prevent continued use of Office resources associated with the excluded practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use or obtaining USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate and shall not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order bars both use and acquisition of identifiers/certificates during exclusion, subject only to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and post disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the exact Notice of Exclusion text to be published and provides the URL for the OED Reading Room where disciplinary decisions are posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures communication of USPTO discipline to other jurisdictions and public stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement process and compliance with § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any request for reinstatement, the respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires strict adherence to the reinstatement procedures and standards set forth in § 11.60 when seeking to resume practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for state disbarment supporting reciprocal exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent's disbarment by the Supreme Court of Washington was for violating Washington State Rules of Professional Conduct (1A, 1.14(a), 8A(b), and 8.5(c)) in connection with handling a European patent application: failure to maintain client funds in an identifiable trust account; commission of a criminal act (theft of client funds) that reflects adversely on the lawyer; and conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific findings of misconduct in the state discipline proceeding formed the factual basis for the USPTO's reciprocal discipline request and the public Notice of Exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority cited for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly cites the federal statute and USPTO regulations that authorize reciprocal discipline and public notice of disciplinary actions.
